questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Horizontal Hyperbola Given an Equation in Expanded Form
questions.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola ${x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}+8x+50y=129?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-5{y}^{2}+8x+50y & =129 \\ {x}^{2}+8x-5{y}^{2}+50y & =129 \\ {x}^{2}+8x-5[{y}^{2}-10y] & =129 \\ (x+4)^{2}-16-5[(y-5)^{2}-25] & =129 \\ (x+4)^{2}-16-5(y-5)^{2}+125 & =129 \\ (x+4)^{2}-5(y-5)^{2} & =129+16-125 \\ (x+4)^{2}-5(y-5)^{2} & =20 \\ \frac{(x+4)^{2}}{20}-\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{4} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center is $(-4,5).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Vertical Hyperbola
questions.problem: What is the center of the hyperbola $\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{9}-(x+4)^{2}=1?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Note that the given equation can be rewritten as follows:

$$
\frac{(y-7)^{2}}{9}-\frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{1}=1
$$

In this case, we have $h=-4$ and $k=7.$

Therefore, the center of the hyperbola is $(-4,7).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Center of a Horizontal Hyperbola Given an Equation in Expanded Form
questions.problem:
What is the center of the hyperbola 
$4{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}-40x+6y=-85?$
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-3{y}^{2}-40x+6y & =-85 \\ 4{x}^{2}-40x-3{y}^{2}+6y & =-85 \\ 4[{x}^{2}-10x]-3[{y}^{2}-2y] & =-85 \\ 4[(x-5)^{2}-25]-3[(y-1)^{2}-1] & =-85 \\ 4(x-5)^{2}-100-3(y-1)^{2}+3 & =-85 \\ 4(x-5)^{2}-3(y-1)^{2} & =12 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{3}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4} & =1 \\ \frac{(x-5)^{2}}{(\sqrt{3})^{2}}-\frac{(y-1)^{2}}{{2}^{2}} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center is $(5,1).$

questions.problem:
The center of the hyperbola $9{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}-36y+8x=4$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$

questions.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-4{x}^{2}-36y+8x & =4 \\ 9{y}^{2}-36y-4{x}^{2}+8x & =4 \\ 9[{y}^{2}-4y]-4[{x}^{2}-2x] & =4 \\ 9[(y-2)^{2}-4]-4[(x-1)^{2}-1] & =4 \\ 9(y-2)^{2}-36-4(x-1)^{2}+4 & =4 \\ 9(y-2)^{2}-4(x-1)^{2} & =4+36-4 \\ 9(y-2)^{2}-4(x-1)^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{(y-2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{9} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-2)^{2}}{{2}^{2}}-\frac{(x-1)^{2}}{{3}^{2}} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,1,2\,).$

questions.problem:

The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}+36y+10x & =25 \\ 9{y}^{2}+36y-{x}^{2}+10x & =25 \\ 9[{y}^{2}+4y]-[{x}^{2}-10x] & =25 \\ 9[(y+2)^{2}-4]-[(x-5)^{2}-25] & =25 \\ 9(y+2)^{2}-36-(x-5)^{2}+25 & =25 \\ 9(y+2)^{2}-(x-5)^{2} & =25+36-25 \\ 9(y+2)^{2}-(x-5)^{2} & =36 \\ \frac{(y+2)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-5)^{2}}{36} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-(-2))^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x-5)^{2}}{36} & =1\end{aligned}
$$
